summary: This article explains why some birds fly huge distances with the changing seasons, how they find their way, and how routes near the Arabian Peninsula connect three continents.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Migratory Birds: Travelers of the Sky” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: a group of living things that are alike and can have young together
an area of land that an animal lives in and often defends
an object or feature that is easy to recognize and helps someone find their way

challengeTerms.def: a regular route that migrating birds follow between their breeding and non-breeding areas
a narrow strip of land or space that connects two areas and is used as a passage
relating to a force, like the one from Earth, that can be sensed and used to find direction

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that animals can find their way across huge distances without any map or GPS? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why the Arabian Peninsula is important to migratory birds.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review species, territory, and landmark, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses flyway, corridor, and magnetic to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
